content.title: Win and you're in: Suns host Warriors in Friday Showdown
content.text: It all comes down to this.Friday night in downtown Phoenix, the Suns will host a win-or-go-home contest that decides the No. 8 seed in the Western Conference.Their opponent? The Golden State Warriors, led by a legendary duo fresh off an emotional comeback victory on Wednesday.The winner will face a quick turnaround, heading to Oklahoma City for a matchup with the defending-champion Thunder. Game 1 of that series will tip off at 12:30pm Pacific.It only makes sense for these two teams to meet in a win-or-go-home scenario. They have both dealt with the injury bug this season and both have a superstar that knows what it takes to win these elimination games.Regular Season SeriesUnlike the Portland matchup earlier this week, the results of this year's meetings between the Warriors and Suns should probably be taken with a grain of salt.Three of the regular season meetings featured Jimmy Butler, who is now sidelined with a torn ACL. None of them included Kristaps Porzingis, the Warriors' new starting center who gives them a five-out spacing element they've been searching for. Porzingis is listed as questionable Friday with right ankle soreness.Among all the Warriors' rotation pieces, only Draymond Green, Brandin Podziemski, and Gui Santos have appeared in all four matchups.On the Suns side, Devin Booker and Dillon Brooks played in three of the four games, with Booker thriving offensively with 33.7 points per game on 50% shooting. He also averaged 9.7 free throw attempts against the Dubs, being physical on his drives and taking advantage of their guard defenders.Nevertheless, Golden State went 3-1 against the Suns, holding Phoenix to just 107.4 points per 100 possessions. If the Suns hope to extend their season and clinch a playoff berth, they will need to look sharper offensively than Tuesday night.The Suns' strengthsIt's rare for any player to see an opponent for the first time during a postseason setting, but this will be Jalen Green's first time facing Golden State this year.It presents an intriguing storyline as Green was part of the Houston Rockets' playoff matchup with the Warriors last April. He will be looking for a little redemption on Friday, hoping to carry over his elite scoring performance from Tuesday.Green's downhill burst might give Golden State significant problems. Sure, they have game-planned against him before ... but last year's Rockets didn't have close to the level of spacing and 3-point shooting that Phoenix can deploy around him.Defensively, the Suns have done a solid job against Curry but also realize his next flurry can happen any time. Curry has averaged 23.7 points against Phoenix this year on 43.5% shooting from two and only 34.4% shooting on threes. Holding him to only 11 three-point makes in 102 total minutes feels like a significant win. You can't ask for anything better.The key will be sustaining that physicality and aggressive perimeter defense without getting into foul trouble, which we saw happen with Booker and Brooks in the first play-in game.In some ways, this matchup plays directly into the Suns' favor, at least stylistically. Phoenix has been one of the league's best defenses at forcing turnovers and turning those mistakes into easy offense. We even saw it come into play during their second-half run against Portland, getting out in transition and scoring before the Blazers had a chance to set their defense.That could spell bad news for Golden State, who has notoriously been a turnover-heavy group. This season, they ranked 26th in that department, turning it over on 15.6% of their possessions. Although it's a trade off the Warriors have been okay living with because Steve Kerr values a high-octane offense with passing and movement, that's a dangerous gamble when your season comes down to 48 minutes.Dillon Brooks, who spoke about the matchup after Thursday's practice, preached the importance of keeping their activity level high. He pointed to how Tuesday's game shifted when they were more physical.Offensive rebounds also play a role, and the Suns will need to dominate the boards in this matchup. When Phoenix grabs 10+ offensive rebounds this year, they are 37-28. When they don't, that record drops to 8-10."It shows that you can stay in games if you get more possessions and create easier shots," Brooks said. "Especially when you're getting steals or blocks and you're able to go down the floor against advantages. That's what we got to hang our hat on."The Warriors' strengthsThis might serve as a "duh" statement, but there is nobody like Stephen Curry and Draymond Green. They are one-of-one in their own respective ways. If there's a team prone to getting hot and flipping a game on its head, it's Golden State – and it's because of the dynamic ball-screen action those two have mastered over the last 14 years.All it takes for Golden State to overcome the odds in a single game is Curry and Green taking over. It was on display against the Clippers, with Green terrorizing Kawhi Leonard down the stretch and making everything difficult for him. If Booker or Brooks have it going for Phoenix, expect Green to willingly take those assignments in the second half.Defensively, expect Gary Payton II to be the type of nuisance Jordan Goodwin is for the Suns. Payton has always been the Warriors' best option on the ball, often playing up a position when needed. Between him and Green (combining for six steals on Wednesday), their active hands could force the Suns into some problems if they over-dribble or aren't protective of the ball.The Warriors also have arguably the best five-out options in basketball with Porzingis and Al Horford spacing on the perimeter to give Curry and Podziemski adequate driving lanes. This is going to be a huge test for the Suns' frontcourt, notably Oso Ighodaro and Mark Williams to not allow those guys to catch the ball with open space. Williams enters Friday listed as questionable with left foot soreness.The Warriors play a totally unique style, focused on their off-ball movement and using Curry's gravity to create opportunities for others. That's where the Suns' discipline will come into play. Suns head coach Jordan Ott knows his team will need to be locked in on every possession."That's the challenge, it just never stops," Ott said. "It's not only just the guy on the ball, it's the screener's defender as well that needs to be super alert. It's going to take five guys, not just one guy ... but you got to do it for all 48 [minutes]. That's the mental resilience you need to have this time of year."The X's and O's will always matter in basketball matchups. But if you ask Brooks, these postseason battles are determined by who wants it more."These games come down to who has the effort and who's going to execute," Brooks said. "That's what it comes down to."
